items.claim: The Prov.7.24 echo is not the unique two-way link the rationale frames it as, and the row's own life/death antithesis leaves an in-span K/Q note undisclosed.
items.evidence: collate.py scores the row's quoted וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י as BYTE tier against both oshb:Prov.8.32 and oshb:Prov.7.24 (the two texts are pointed-byte-identical for these four words: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י = וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י). But sweep.py --skel on that same four-word string returns 3 verses book-wide, not 2: Prov.5.7, Prov.7.24, Prov.8.32. The row names only the 7:24 parallel and calls it 'the poem's own closing frame' reproducing 7:24 'almost word for word', without disclosing the identical incipit at 5:7 (oshb:Prov.5.7) that opens a separate, earlier lecture unit -- a same-count-different-set gap that weakens the claim of a deliberate two-way frame specific to chapter 7. Separately, the row's own closing antithesis argument quotes web:Prov.8.35 ('whoever finds me finds life') but oshb:Prov.8.35 carries a ketiv/qere note (pmarks_Prov.json kq['Prov.8.35']=1: the inline unpointed ketiv token precedes the pointed qere in the verse's own bytes, כִּ֣י מֹ֭צְאִי מצאי מָצָ֣א חַיִּ֑ים וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה) that the row never discloses, despite the span-relevant K/Q disclosure rule being unconditional and this verse sitting inside the row's own argued span (8:32-8:36).

items.claim: Hebrew verb concord across 9:1-9:6 confirms personified Wisdom is the continuous grammatical subject through the narration and into her own quoted invitation.
items.evidence: All governing verbs of 9:1-9:3 are 3fs, matching the single feminine subject חכמות of oshb:Prov.9.1 (skeleton tier) straight through the sending and the calling itself in 9:3 -- the calling verb is 3fs, not 3fp, so Wisdom herself remains the one who 'calls' even though she has sent her maidens ahead; the WEB rendering (web:Prov.9.3, 'She has sent out her maidens. She cries...') keeps the same subject assignment, so this is not a translation-only artifact. The invitation's own first-person verb in 9:5 and the 3fs אָ֣מְרָה ('she said') of 9:4 close the same voice. Front-seam petuchah at oshb:Prov.8.36 (single-witness) is correctly placed, and the rejected_alternative correctly declines to extend the span to the petuchah recorded at Prov.9.9, since that mark falls after the subject/mood change at 9:7.

items.claim: The mood shift the row argues -- participial 9:7 to command-form 9:8-9 to nominal 9:10 -- holds at the pointed-byte level, and the closing petuchah is correctly placed.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.9.7 (יֹ֤סֵ֨ר לֵ֗ץ לֹקֵ֣חַֽ ל֣וֹ קָל֑וֹן וּמוֹכִ֖יחַ לְרָשָׁ֣ע מוּמֽוֹ) carries participle forms (the corrector/reprover pair), matching the row's 'participial maxim' description. oshb:Prov.9.8 (אַל תּ֣וֹכַח לֵ֭ץ פֶּן יִשְׂנָאֶ֑ךָּ הוֹכַ֥ח לְ֝חָכָ֗ם וְיֶאֱהָבֶֽךָּ) and oshb:Prov.9.9 (תֵּ֣ן לְ֭חָכָם וְיֶחְכַּם ע֑וֹד הוֹדַ֥ע לְ֝צַדִּ֗יק וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶֽקַח) supply true 2ms imperatives (הוכח, תן, הודע); the negative command אל תוכח in the same verse is technically a negated jussive/imperfect rather than a true imperative -- Biblical Hebrew has no dedicated negative-imperative form, so both are command-mood and the row's collapsing of the two under 'imperative core' does not affect the mood-shift boundary it argues. oshb:Prov.9.10 (תְּחִלַּ֣ת חָ֭כְמָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים בִּינָֽה) is a fully verbless nominal clause, confirming the row's 'without an imperative verb' description of the following span. Petuchah at oshb:Prov.9.9 (single-witness) correctly closes this span.

items.claim: 9:10-9:12's verbless thesis, first-person echo, and conditional close all verify against the pointed bytes, and the row discloses rather than hides the cross-seam echo back to 9:1-9:6.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.9.10 (תְּחִלַּ֣ת חָ֭כְמָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים בִּינָֽה) is verbless; oshb:Prov.9.11's בי ('by me', skeleton tier) is genuinely 1cs; oshb:Prov.9.12 (אִם חָ֭כַמְתָּ חָכַ֣מְתָּ לָּ֑ךְ וְ֝לַ֗צְתָּ לְֽבַדְּךָ֥ תִשָּֽׂא) opens with the conditional participle-clause the row describes -- all three match the row's claims. The row explicitly names the first-person echo of Wisdom's 9:1-9:6 voice rather than concealing it, satisfying the disclosure standard for a byte-true device that straddles a row's own boundary rather than counting silently against it. Front-seam petuchah at oshb:Prov.9.9 (single-witness), the verse immediately preceding this span, is correctly cited.

items.claim: The claimed 9:16/9:4 invitation-formula echo is byte-identical for the shared opening and the sweep count is exhaustive; the closing petuchah is correctly placed.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel on מי פתי יסר הנה returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Prov.9.4 and oshb:Prov.9.16, matching the row's claimed pair with no undisclosed third hit. The underlying pointed source text (verse_map_oshb.json) is byte-identical for the shared opening: מִי פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה = מִי פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה -- stronger than the row's own 'shares its opening four consonantal words' framing. New subject אשת כסילות (oshb:Prov.9.13, skeleton tier) is confirmed. Petuchah at oshb:Prov.9.18 (single-witness) correctly closes both this span and the eight-collection first unit, matching the book's own collection-seam data.

items.claim: The verse-initial mishle count of exactly two is confirmed by an independent sweep that also reproduces the toolkit's own same-count-different-set trap (3 anywhere vs 2 verse-initial), which the row correctly avoided.
items.evidence: prov_device_inventory.json's mishle_verse_initial entry lists exactly Prov.1.1 and Prov.10.1 (count 2); an independent sweep.py --skel of משלי anywhere in the book returns 3 verses (Prov.1.1, Prov.10.1, Prov.25.1), confirming the row's careful use of 'verse-initial' rather than the larger anywhere-count -- 25:1's occurrence sits mid-verse (the gam-elleh header interior), not verse-initial, exactly the hazard the toolkit names. Petuchah at oshb:Prov.9.18 and oshb:Prov.10.1 (both single-witness) are correctly disclosed as bracketing the seam.

items.claim: The B-line repetition the row cites between 10:6 and 10:11 is byte-identical, not merely skeleton-matched, and the sweep confirms no undisclosed third occurrence.
items.evidence: collate.py scores the row's quoted ופי רשעים יכסה חמס at skeleton tier against its own citation, but the underlying pointed bytes show the B-lines of oshb:Prov.10.6 and oshb:Prov.10.11 are fully byte-identical (וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְכַסֶּ֥ה חָמָֽס), stronger than the row's own claim. sweep.py --skel of the same string returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, matching the row's 'five verses on' non-adjacent pair with no hidden third hit. The row's claim that 10:7 shares neither the head/blessing nor mouth/violence pairing is confirmed: oshb:Prov.10.7 contains no rosh or peh/chamas tokens.

items.claim: The memory/name antithesis and both boundary non-overlaps (10:6 head/mouth, 10:8 heart/lips) are confirmed directly from the pointed bytes.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.10.7 (זֵ֣כֶר צַ֭דִּיק לִבְרָכָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֖ם רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִרְקָֽב) matches the row's memory/name antithesis (זכר צדיק / שם רשעים) exactly. oshb:Prov.10.8 (חֲכַם לֵ֭ב יִקַּ֣ח מִצְוֺ֑ת וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט) confirms the heart/lips imagery the row cites as absent from 10:7's own vocabulary; oshb:Prov.10.6 (בְּ֭רָכוֹת לְרֹ֣אשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְכַסֶּ֥ה חָמָֽס) confirms the head/mouth pairing is likewise absent from 10:7. The righteous/wicked terms do recur across all three verses (10:6-10:8), but that is the antithetic collection's stock frame vocabulary rather than a distinguishing catchword, consistent with the book's stoplist-filtered catchword counts for this chapter.
